description: Version bumps for the pins nobody would otherwise refresh: the Dart packages and their lockfile, the Flutter toolchain in .tool-versions, and the workflow actions.
Renovate opens one pull request per group, weekly, and stops; review, CI and the merge desk take it from there like any other.
minimumReleaseAge is the cool-down: nothing younger than three days is proposed.

constraints.flutter is the Flutter Renovate regenerates pubspec.lock with. Renovate does not read .tool-versions, and left alone it would use the newest Flutter, which can resolve a lock the pinned one cannot. The Flutter toolchain pull request moves it together with .tool-versions and the manifest's surface line (the regex managers below), and dev/verify.sh checks it equals .tool-versions.

lockFileMaintenance.description: Every pubspec.yaml constraint is a caret range the newest release already satisfies, so without this the versions pinned in pubspec.lock would never move. One weekly pull request regenerates the lock within those ranges.

packageRules.description: The Flutter SDK in .tool-versions is what CI and a local mise install both build with, releases included: its own pull request, never part of a package group.
Workflows outside .github run on the forge's runner, which is not GitHub: a newer action major can need a newer node than it has. Digest refreshes only there.

customManagers.description: The dependency desk's manifest (upstreams.yml) names the Flutter version in its surface line, and a bump must update it in the same pull request. This reads that version, so the Flutter toolchain pull request moves it with .tool-versions.
constraints.flutter above, so the Flutter toolchain pull request moves it with .tool-versions too.
